This directly conflicts with this milestone's Part 8-10 requirements and must be resolved (either by extending the code with a resume path analogous to B2N's, or by explicitly authorizing a design where a fresh empty ledger is required for every future attempt) before ANY live execution -- it is a genuine engineering gap, not something this preflight can paper over.

part8_9_10_ledger_and_resume_design.status: DESIGN PROPOSED, NOT IMPLEMENTED -- this is the single largest gap between B2Z's current code and this milestone's required safety bar
part8_9_10_ledger_and_resume_design.reasoning_for_new_run_id: B2N's run_id (b2n-p3e-98695fbdf44146c93ff08c8c) is exhausted (20/20, 0 remaining) and scoped to a DIFFERENT contract (migration-lineage-only, 1 request/member). B2Z needs its own independent authorization, budget, and ledger identity -- never reuse B2N's exhausted budget.
proposed_authorization_object_fields: run_id (new, derived deterministically from a B2Z-specific seed analogous to B2N's derivation)
manifest_digest (bound to the same 82bbda32... B2N manifest)
projection_digest (bound to the existing eb2713e3... frozen projection)
part8_9_10_ledger_and_resume_design.request_stage_identity_proposal: each physical attempt must be tagged with an explicit stage name distinguishing the three sequential calls per member -- proposed names matching the existing Attempt.member_request_number semantics: MIGRATION_TX (member_request_number=1), CREATOR_HISTORY (member_request_number=2), FUNDING_TX (member_request_number=3)
required_code_change_for_resume: Add a resume-capable entry point analogous to B2N's resume_run(): read the existing (possibly non-empty) PhysicalAttemptLedger, determine the highest completed (ordinal, stage) pair, and compute the deterministic next (ordinal, stage) to attempt.

Because a member's 3 stages depend on each other's RESPONSE CONTENT (not just success/failure), a resume implementation must persist enough of each stage's parsed output (creator address after stage 1, candidate signature after stage 2) to resume mid-member without re-deriving it from a lost response -- the current Attempt dataclass does NOT carry this (it has target/outcome/error_class but no parsed creator/candidate fields). This is a real design gap: B2N's resume worked because each member was a single independent request; B2Z's resume is harder because of intra-member sequential dependency.

Proposed minimal fix: extend the per-member ledger entry (or a parallel small JSON side-file, append-only, keyed by ordinal) to durably record {ordinal, stage, resolved_creator (after stage 1), migration_time (after stage 1), candidate_signature (after stage 2)} the moment each stage succeeds -- so a resume can reconstruct the exact next request's params without re-fetching an already-completed stage.

Pre-dispatch durable reservation (an ATTEMPT_RESERVED-equivalent event written BEFORE the network call) must be added -- B2Z's current _call() only appends to the ledger AFTER the attempt completes (success or failure), which means a crash DURING a network call leaves ZERO ledger evidence of the attempt, unlike B2N's PreDispatchEventLedger which durably reserves first. This is a second real gap versus B2N's durability lessons (Part 9's explicit requirement).
part8_9_10_ledger_and_resume_design.duplicate_stage_prevention_proposal: mirror B2N's DurableAccountingClient pattern: refuse to re-dispatch a (ordinal, stage) pair that already has a terminal event in the durable ledger
part8_9_10_ledger_and_resume_design.explicit_conclusion: Building this resume-capable design properly is real engineering work, not something to fabricate as already-existing. This preflight documents the design; it does not claim the design is implemented or tested. A safe path forward is to execute B2Z's EXISTING all-or-nothing runner (which the code and tests already qualify) for a SINGLE session, accepting that a stop mid-run requires manual ledger archival + fresh start for the remainder -- OR to invest in the resume extension first. This choice is presented as a decision point, not resolved unilaterally here.

part11_creator_funding_evidence_contract.candidate_funding_transaction_requiremen: a signature from getSignaturesForAddress(creator) with blockTime < migration_time, selected as the single most-recent qualifying candidate (candidates[0])
part11_creator_funding_evidence_contract.funding_source_requirement: the transaction's parsed System Program transfer/transferWithSeed instruction (top-level or nested in meta.innerInstructions) with info.destination == creator and integer info.lamports > 0 -- the 'source' field is NOT itself validated or required to be present in the funding_edge check (proves_inbound_sol_funding does not assert on info.source)

part11_creator_funding_evidence_contract.confidence_state: binary only -- evidence_observed=true and provenance_complete=true are set together only on full 3-stage success; there is no partial-confidence or lower-tier evidence state in this contract

part12_temporal_semantics.lookback_window: UNBOUNDED -- getSignaturesForAddress uses only {limit: 1000}, no before/until timestamp bound; the client-side filter (blockTime < migration_time) is the ONLY temporal constraint, applied to whatever signatures the 1000-row page happens to contain
part12_temporal_semantics.ordering: getSignaturesForAddress returns signatures in reverse-chronological order (Solana RPC default) -- the client code takes the list as-given and filters, so candidates[0] after filtering is the MOST RECENT signature strictly before migration_time
part12_temporal_semantics.same_slot_semantics: not explicitly handled -- if a funding transaction and the migration transaction occurred in the same slot but funding's blockTime happens to equal migration's blockTime (same-second resolution), the strict < comparison would exclude it. blockTime has only 1-second resolution on Solana, so same-second-different-order transactions are a real, if narrow, edge case the code does not specially address.
part12_temporal_semantics.multiple_candidate_handling: NONE beyond taking the single most-recent qualifying signature -- if that specific transaction's parsed content fails proves_inbound_sol_funding() (e.g. it turns out to be a token transfer, or funds someone else), the ENTIRE member fails via B2Z_FIRST_NON_SUCCESS_STOP_NO_FUNDING_EDGE. There is NO fallback to try candidates[1], candidates[2], etc. This is a real precision/recall tradeoff in the existing contract, not something this preflight is introducing.
part12_temporal_semantics.no_candidate_behavior: member fails immediately via B2Z_FIRST_NON_SUCCESS_STOP_NO_CANDIDATE if the filtered candidate list is empty

part13_multiple_funding_candidates.current_code_behavior: as documented in Part 12 -- only the single most-recent pre-migration signature is ever attempted; no ranking, no retry across candidates, no self-funding exclusion, no CEX/service-wallet exclusion, no SOL-vs-token disambiguation before dispatch (disambiguation only happens post-fetch, and failure there kills the whole member)
part13_multiple_funding_candidates.self_funding_risk: NOT excluded by the code -- if a creator's own wallet or a wallet they control sent the 'funding' transaction to itself in a way that satisfies proves_inbound_sol_funding's destination check, it would pass. The coverage matrix (Part 4/5) flagged ordinals 8, 11, 15, 19 as having unusually wide local funder fan-outs (52, 510, 47, 53 rows) resembling known distribution/subprov patterns from prior WATCHTOWER classification work -- these are exactly the members most likely to trip this gap if the most-recent-pre-migration signature happens to be a dust/distribution transfer rather than a genuine funding relationship.
part13_multiple_funding_candidates.service_exchange_wallet_handling: NOT distinguished -- no CEX/service address list is consulted anywhere in b2z_execution_boundary.py
part13_multiple_funding_candidates.token_vs_sol_transfers: explicitly distinguished -- proves_inbound_sol_funding only accepts program=='system' transfer/transferWithSeed instructions; an SPL token transfer (program=='spl-token') is correctly excluded (proven by test_funding_parser_requires_positive_inbound_system_sol_transfer)
part13_multiple_funding_candidates.failed_transactions: excluded at the _result() layer for BOTH migration and funding transactions (meta.err must be null)
part13_multiple_funding_candidates.irrelevant_transactions: excluded only via the destination==creator + lamports>0 + timestamp check -- an SOL transfer that satisfies all three checks but happens to be unrelated fan-out dust would still pass
part13_multiple_funding_candidates.explicit_flag_for_this_milestone: the existing contract does NOT let B2Z silently choose among multiple candidates using an undocumented rule -- it deterministically picks the single most recent one and has a hard pass/fail gate. But this preflight explicitly notes the candidate-selection logic is UNSOPHISTICATED relative to the known funding-pattern complexity documented elsewhere in this repository (treasury-vs-subprov, distribution fan-out, self-funding schemes) -- live execution results for the flagged wide-fan-out ordinals should be reviewed with extra scrutiny before being treated as ground truth.

blockers: B2ZRunner has no resume/continuation mechanism (Part 8-10) -- a live run must currently be all-or-nothing across all 20 members and 60 requests, or require manual ledger archival to retry the remainder from scratch. This is a genuine capability gap versus B2N's qualified resume design, not something this preflight can resolve without either (a) accepting the all-or-nothing risk for a single execution session, or (b) authorizing a separate implementation milestone for B2Z resume support first.

B2ZRunner has no pre-dispatch durable reservation (writes to the ledger only AFTER each attempt completes) -- a crash mid-network-call would leave zero ledger evidence of that specific attempt, unlike B2N's ATTEMPT_RESERVED-before-dispatch pattern.

Candidate-selection logic (Part 13) is unsophisticated relative to known funding-pattern complexity in this repository (self-funding, distribution fan-out, subprov hubs) -- 4 of 20 members (ordinals 8, 11, 15, 19) show wide local funder fan-out patterns that warrant extra scrutiny of their live B2Z results before treating them as ground truth.
verdict_reasoning: The B2Z contract, request shape, cohort binding, evidence/temporal/candidate semantics, storage impact, and production-authority scope are all fully resolved directly from the existing qualified code and tests -- no ambiguity remains in what B2Z does or requires. Local evidence coverage was exhaustively searched and found genuinely insufficient for all 20 members (not assumed), so the full 60-request budget is the correct, measured requirement, matching (not exceeding) the existing MAX_REQUESTS=60 contract. The blockers listed above are real and must be weighed as part of the GO/NO-GO decision, but they do not represent unresolved AMBIGUITY in what B2Z needs or how much it costs -- they represent a genuine safety/robustness gap in the CURRENT B2Z code (no resume, no pre-dispatch durability) that the human authorizing execution should explicitly accept or address first.
